% glossaries with hyperref and a table of contents: a \gls in a heading,
% which hyperref's link in the table of contents holds too. With the toc
% option, each glossary is in the table of contents; the symbols glossary
% has an entry used only in a description, so its heading first appears
% after the second makeglossaries run. (A blank line before
% \printglossaries: a \phantomsection in a paragraph puts the anchor in the
% paragraph, for any heading.)
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\usepackage[toc,symbols]{glossaries}
\makeglossaries
\newglossaryentry{unit}{type=symbols,name={u},
  description={the identity of a group}}
\newglossaryentry{group}{name={group},
  description={a set with an associative operation and a \gls{unit}}}
\begin{document}
\tableofcontents
\section{Every \gls{group}}
A \gls{group} again.

\printglossaries
\end{document}
